content: When I open a Lean file in VSCode, it automatically starts up a Lean server for that file for me. Is there a way to disable this behavior?
the infoview window isn't open but the Lean server is still starting up
I have even seen lean start up on my Mac when I open a latex file

Aaron Liu said:

When I open a Lean file in VSCode, it automatically starts up a Lean server for that file for me. Is there a way to disable this behavior?

Disable the Lean extension.

Kevin Buzzard said:

I have even seen lean start up on my Mac when I open a latex file

Was the LaTeX file in a Lean project?
I think Aaron would like the dumb regex syntax highlighting without the server

Marc Huisinga said:

Was the LaTeX file in a Lean project?

It was not, although I have not seen this behaviour for the last month or two. It was happening regularly in Jan/Feb on my mac (but not on my linux machine) when I was writing my FLT course. I only use VS Code for Lean but I was experimenting with using it for LaTeX too and was amused to find that Lean would just start up anyway :-) I'll look out for it happening again but right now this is not an issue (and I cannot reproduce any more).

Marc Huisinga said:

Was the LaTeX file in a Lean project?

Aah! The actual answer is "not as far as I was concerned, but there was a spurious lakefile.toml in $HOME".

Marc Huisinga said:

Disable the Lean extension.

This also gets rid of the dropdown menu that has the option to turn on the Lean server :(
just ran into this issue again, it's very annoying because I have to wait for the Lean server to start up before I can shut it off again
